title: Redd Foxx's loyalty to old entertainers
summary: Hinton and Maxwell admire Foxx's help for old performers and wish his show had Black writers.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, you've done so many beautiful things. And Redd Foxx is a wonderful, powerful man. Throughout the whole black community we have such respect for him for when he finally made it and got to be a star, he went back and pulled out all the old entertainers. Just so beautiful.
Yeah, I know. Aunt Louise, is that her name? She used to be a snake dancer or something in some little club? He's got all his old buddies there.
He put them all out and (inaudible).
Well, black or white I think that's a great thing to do.
And most people seem to forget that but he found jobs for them. And he remembered the funny things they had done and got them in some spot where --

And he did. They're all great. The only thing wrong with that show is they got white writers because, you know, it's a white situation comedy with black actors. That was always a big disappointment to me. Black humor is so great, you know, that it's a pity that they don't have real black humor on there.
It has to be like jazz, it has to be improvised. A great deal of it has to be improvised and
Redd is really king of that.
Yeah, you know, he's great at what he's doing but he's a thousand times greater than that if they'd just let him go, you know.
Well, there were some good experiences, Jimmy.
Well, you know, you do a little here and a little there.
